transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess for the past year or so, I've been having some issues staying on track at work. 

Just... the smallest things pull me off what I’m doing before I can stop it. Like a phone buzz, or somebody walking past my office. Or even just some random thought about my in-laws. It just takes my attention away. So... yeah. That's what brings me in.
Besides having trouble focusing, do you find yourself feeling restless or fidgety, or do you tend to act without thinking things through?

I don't know... maybe a little. In meetings, mostly. 

I guess I'm usually bouncing my knee, or clicking a pen... shifting around in my chair. I don't always notice it, but people have started giving me these looks. Like they think I'm trying to rush them. Even when I'm really just trying to listen to what they're saying. So... yeah, I guess I get a bit restless.

When you think back to your school years—elementary, middle, and high school—did you have similar problems with attention and staying focused, or is this something that's really just started in the past year?

Um... yeah, I suppose it's not just the past year. Looking back... it was kind of like that when I was a kid, too. 

My teachers were always moving my seat around. They said I talked too much... or I'd just get up without asking. I guess I had a habit of blurting things out before they even finished a question. So... yeah. It's been around.

You mentioned these attention and restlessness issues have affected your work and were noticed by teachers in school—have they also caused problems in your personal relationships or other important areas of your life?

Um... I mean, I'm still keeping up overall. Things are mostly fine. But... yeah, I guess it causes some issues. 

It's starting to cost me some trust at home. Just... when family plans don't go the way they should, my wife gets frustrated. And at work, people are losing patience with me. Like in meetings, or... mentoring conversations. It just... yeah. It causes some friction when things don't go how they're supposed to. That's about it.
When you think about those early school years—say, around age 6 or 7—do you remember having these kinds of attention and restlessness problems back then, or did they start a bit later?
I don't really know. That was a long time ago. I guess... maybe? I just remember getting in trouble a lot. But I couldn't tell you exactly how old I was when it started.

You mentioned some friction at work and at home—but thinking about it overall, would you say these attention and restlessness problems have significantly interfered with your ability to do your job well, or to maintain good relationships with your family?

I mean... like I said a minute ago, I'm still keeping up overall. It's not like I can't do my job. 

Just... yeah, it costs me some trust at home when family plans get derailed. And at work, people lose patience with me during meetings or... those mentoring conversations. But I wouldn't say it's completely stopped me from doing what I need to do. I'm still managing.

When you think about everything together—the attention problems, the restlessness, the issues at work and at home—would you say these things are causing you real difficulty in your daily life, or are they more like minor annoyances that don't really get in your way?

I guess... they're not just minor annoyances. But it's not like my life is falling apart either. Like I said, I'm still keeping up overall. It's just... yeah, it's starting to cost me trust at home when family plans get messed up. And at work, people are losing patience with me when things don't go the way they should in meetings or mentoring conversations. So... it's somewhere in the middle, I suppose.
When you were in elementary school—say, around ages 6 to 12—did your teachers or parents ever mention concerns about you having trouble paying attention, or being overly active or impulsive?

Yeah... I suppose. Like I said before, I got in trouble a lot back then. Teachers were always... moving my seat. 

They complained that I talked too much, or that I'd just get up without asking. I guess I also had a habit of... blurting things out before they even finished asking a question. So, yeah... they brought it up.
